licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets cover the dominant clusters: fraudulent license procurement; criminal convictions; clinical incompetence/negligence; substance abuse/impairment; independent mental/physical incapacity; broader unprofessional/unethical conduct (sexual misconduct, patient abandonment, boundary violations, etc.); falsification of or failures around records and mandatory reporting; prior discipline or adverse action in another jurisdiction; and catch-all statutory/regulatory/board-order violations that don't fit the more specific practice-conduct buckets.

profession_specific.license_tiers.rationale: The data clusters into three core licensed nurse tiers (RN, LPN, APRN umbrella), the four named APRN specialties that many states enumerate separately (NP, CNM, CRNA, CNS), plus two support/paraprofessional categories (nursing assistants/aides and medication aides/other allied roles like administrators) that appear across a minority of states.

profession_specific.lpn_supervision_requ.rationale: The items are supervisor types, which cluster tightly into RN, APRN, physician (MD/DO/osteopath/naturopath), physician assistant, dentist, podiatrist, and optometrists/chiropractors (other eye/spine specialists), with a residual bucket for broad catch-all statutory phrases like 'any licensed health care provider authorized by state law'.

profession_specific.controlled_substance.rationale: The data clusters naturally by DEA schedule level, with Schedule II warranting a split between unrestricted and restricted/conditional grants (supply limits, drug-type limits, credential requirements), plus a handful of items covering non-controlled or legend drugs and shorthand range entries spanning multiple schedules.
